findings.issue: The stem has no API version. From API 67.0, plain 'insert rec;' also runs in user mode (the running user's object and field permissions), and a class with no sharing keyword runs with sharing, so option C is defensible on a current org.
findings.fix: Replace option C with a call that never enforces the user's access, such as 'insert as system rec;', or change the stem to 'Which call enforces the running user's object, field and sharing permissions whatever the class's API version?'

findings.issue: Options-only S hit: the key is the only option that names a specific field setting; the others are flat 'never', 'always' or an unrelated attribute.
findings.fix: Write the wrong options in the same form, each naming a field setting: 'Field set as External ID only', 'Field set as Unique and case-sensitive', 'Field set as Required and External ID'.

findings.issue: Options-only S hit: 'Spawn its own threads' is the odd one out among three everyday Apex features, so it can be picked without knowing the guide's list.
findings.fix: Use plausible capabilities as wrong options, for example 'Run asynchronously in a queue', 'Parse JSON from a callout', 'Call another class's static method'.

findings.issue: Stem says the static variable is set in @TestSetup; the guide says a change made in the setup method does not persist either, so 'The original value' could be read as the value @TestSetup set, which the next test method does not see.
findings.fix: Change the key to 'The value from its initializer' or the stem to 'A static variable is initialized to 5. A test method changes it to 9. What does the next test method see?'

findings.issue: Correct and versioned, but the real exam is said by guides to align to an earlier release (Winter '25), where a class without a sharing keyword usually runs without sharing and Apex runs in system mode. Candidates may meet the old default on the exam.
findings.fix: Optionally add one sentence to each explanation giving the API 66.0-and-earlier behavior, so candidates know both.
